claim: Israel prevented Iran from developing nuclear weapons
reason: Israeli and U.S. strikes severely damaged declared nuclear facilities, but preventing weapon development is a causal/counterfactual conclusion not established by the damage evidence alone

claim: Without the strikes on Iran, 'we'd all be dead'
reason: Counterfactual and not reproducibly falsifiable

claim: Many leaders who walked out privately thanked Israel for taking out Iran's nukes
reason: Private conversations are not independently verifiable from available public evidence

claim: Before the 1967 war Israel was not in the West Bank, Gaza or Golan Heights
reason: Israel captured these territories during the June 1967 war

claim: Three Arab armies were about to invade Israel in 1967
reason: Egypt, Jordan and Syria mobilised and war conditions escalated, but whether a coordinated invasion was imminent remains historically contested; Israel initiated hostilities on 5 June

claim: Israel fought a seven-front war
reason: Depends on a non-standard definition of 'front'

claim: Israel and the United States crushed Iran's army, navy, air force and nuclear facilities
reason: Nuclear facilities were severely damaged and Iranian forces suffered losses, but the categorical claim about entire armed-service branches is broader than available evidence

claim: The bulk of Hezbollah's roughly 150,000 rockets and missiles is gone
reason: Hezbollah's arsenal is documented as substantially diminished, but the precise 'bulk' share and 150,000 baseline are not independently established in this pass

claim: There are thousands of Palestinian terrorist attacks per year against Israelis in the West Bank
reason: Requires a fixed definition of attack and an agreed incident dataset

claim: Settler violence is committed by only about 150 offenders
reason: No reliable public evidence located for a total-offender denominator; incident counts are much larger but do not directly measure unique offenders

claim: Settler violence causes only two or three deaths
reason: UN OCHA recorded 12 Palestinians killed by Israeli settlers by 11 May 2026 and substantially more settler-linked fatalities later in the year

claim: Israel and the United States brought back every remaining hostage
reason: Requires reconciliation with the official hostage ledger as of the speech date before scoring

claim: Qatar has spent billions funding U.S. universities and media
reason: Billions in Qatari-linked university gifts/contracts are documented over time and $1.1bn was disclosed in 2025 alone; the broader media component is not established by the same evidence

claim: Qatar's purpose was to make young people hate Israel, America and the West
reason: Motive claim not established by funding totals

claim: Erdogan has murdered thousands of Kurdish civilians
reason: Serious personal-attribution claim requiring conflict-casualty evidence and a defensible attribution standard

claim: Erdogan denies the Armenian genocide
reason: Turkey under Erdogan rejects the genocide legal/historical characterisation, while acknowledging wartime deaths

claim: Erdogan holds the world record for imprisoning journalists and opposition leaders
reason: Turkey has a severe press-freedom record and was historically described as the world's biggest jailer of journalists, but 2026 RSF data do not support a current world-record claim

claim: Turkey illegally occupies Northern Cyprus
reason: UN resolutions reject the secessionist entity and UN records repeatedly describe northern Cyprus as under foreign occupation; the wording is a legal characterisation and should be attributed to the applicable international framework

claim: Hamas used hospitals, schools and mosques as command posts
reason: Evidence exists for militant use of some civilian sites, but a blanket formulation across categories and locations requires case-specific proof

claim: Hamas stole much of the food entering Gaza
reason: A USAID review of 156 aid-loss incidents found no evidence of systematic Hamas diversion of U.S.-funded humanitarian aid; this does not prove zero diversion but does not support 'much' as stated

claim: Israel sent millions of texts, made millions of calls and dropped millions of leaflets warning Gaza civilians
reason: Warning practices are documented, but the exact millions-level totals require independently auditable counts

claim: Israel enabled distribution of two million tons of food into Gaza
reason: Large aid inflows are documented, but this exact cumulative two-million-ton figure was not independently established in the first pass

claim: Israel gave one million polio vaccinations to Gaza's population
reason: More than one million vaccine doses were administered across two rounds, but the campaign was run by WHO, UNICEF, UNRWA, the Palestinian Ministry of Health and partners; Israel facilitated humanitarian pauses rather than 'giving' the vaccinations itself

claim: Israel did more to prevent civilian casualties than any military in history
reason: Comparative superlative lacks a reproducible historical metric

claim: Israel did not commit genocide in Gaza
reason: This is a legal conclusion and should be tied to final competent-court findings rather than ordinary factual scoring

claim: Israel prevented genocide against itself
reason: Counterfactual and legal claim

claim: Jews in New York have become less safe since Mamdani became mayor
reason: Requires a defined antisemitic-incident or crime metric, a fixed baseline and causal attribution

claim: Mamdani praised people convicted of supporting Hamas
reason: Specific allegation requires primary-source verification of the statements and underlying convictions

claim: Mamdani hosted a journalist who filmed abuse of Israeli hostages and withheld footage
reason: Specific allegation requires primary-source verification and evidence about knowledge/withholding

claim: Mamdani's wife liked posts praising October 7 and saying Tel Aviv should not exist
reason: Requires preserved primary social-media evidence and account-authenticity verification
